newsitem.title: UK: German cruise cuts short holiday after grounding.
newsitem.headline: German cruise cuts short holiday after grounding.

text.p: About 500 German tourists had their holiday cruise cut short on Saturday after their ship was holed off Britain's Scilly Isles.
"The paying passengers are getting restless and they are being brought ashore," a coastguard official said as the 25,000-tonne Albatross was left stranded off southwestern England.

"She is still at anchor. The owners have charted a ferry to bring the passengers ashore (to the Scilly Isles). The ship is safe. Divers are looking at it. There is some damage but no danger," he told Reuters.
It was believed that the ship may have struck on the bottom of the harbour some containers that spilled from a cargo ship which sank off the Scilly Isles last month.
Another possibility was that the 39-year-old Nassau-registered ship may have hit the bottom after a guide buoy was moved by rough seas.
The Albatross had set sail from the German port of Bremerhaven and was on a two-week tour of the British isles.
